$note: GRU953 benchmark criteria. Written and frozen BEFORE the rebuilt kit exists, so it can be graded honestly rather than to a target it already knows the answer to. Each criterion names the test that decides it. baseline_verdict is evaluated against the CURRENT (13 Aug 2026) kit, before this rebuild -- most are deliberately 'gap', because that gap is the reason the rebuild exists. target_verdict is filled in during the three convergence rounds once the rebuilt artefact exists to test.
rule: A criterion's statement may not be reworded after this file is committed. If a criterion turns out wrong, retire it (status: retired, with a reason) and add a new one with a new id -- never edit the wording of an existing one, or the three convergence rounds stop being comparable.

criteria.statement: GRU953's own architecture document states, in its own words, whether it is a design system, a brand book, or both, and does not claim to be one while actually being the other.
criteria.test: grep 02_strategy/*.md and the guidebook for the words 'design system' and 'brand book' used with a stated definition
criteria.baseline_note: BRAND-SPEC.md and DESIGN-RULES.md exist but neither states this distinction explicitly.

criteria.statement: The two-tier architecture (GRU953 governs developer-facing surfaces; products get their own identity with GRU953 as endorsement) is written down as a rule, with the endorsement form stated, before any product uses it.
criteria.test: a committed 02_strategy/ARCHITECTURE.md exists and states the endorsement form
criteria.baseline_note: BRAND-SPEC.md §9 states endorsement form for products under GRU953, but nothing states the two-tier split (GRU953 vs independently-branded consumer products) confirmed in this rebuild's interview.

criteria.statement: Design system and brand book are described as two different things, and neither Apple nor Google is cited as publishing a brand book they do not publish.
criteria.test: grep the guidebook and BENCHMARK.md for phrases like "Apple's brand book" or "Google's brand guidelines" used to mean identity governance
criteria.baseline_note: The old kit's RESEARCH.md and DESIGN-RULES.md make no such claim about Apple or Google. Verified this is still correct: Apple's HIG is a design system with no public brand book (only a trademark-permission policy); Google's Material is a design system, and its public brand page is likewise a trademark-usage guide, not identity governance.

criteria.statement: Where GRU953 claims a company publishes both a design system and a brand book (as a model to follow), that claim is backed by a verified finding naming both artefacts.
criteria.test: cross-reference every such claim against findings.json
criteria.baseline_note: The old kit makes no such claim yet; criterion applies once the new guidebook cites these examples.

criteria.statement: The accepted 'GRU = Gated Recurrent Unit' reading risk is stated in the guidebook, with the mitigation rule (tagline always under the wordmark), not quietly dropped.
criteria.test: grep the guidebook for 'Gated Recurrent Unit'
criteria.baseline_note: BRAND-SPEC.md §7 and RESEARCH.md §1 both state this already, well.

criteria.statement: GRU953 states honestly that its own benchmark rests on published guidance, not on how well the benchmarked organisations follow their own guidance, and not on their private brand books.
criteria.test: the benchmark document contains an explicit limits section saying this
criteria.baseline_note: No such limits statement exists yet in the old kit.

criteria.statement: No corner radius, percentage or squircle value is attributed to Apple anywhere in the kit; where a radius is used, it is labelled a GRU953 house choice.
criteria.test: grep the whole tree for 'squircle' or a radius number near the word 'Apple'
criteria.baseline_note: 03_logo/GRU953-appicon.svg's own <desc> reads "at the squircle corner radius iOS and Android expect" and 02_strategy/DESIGN-RULES.md §2.3 repeats it. Confirmed invented: Apple's own HIG states only that masking 'precisely matches the curvature of other rounded interface elements ... and the bezel of the physical device itself' -- no number, ever.

criteria.statement: The rebuilt mark's small-size floor (16px, per the owner's own stated floor) is proven by rasterising and checking counter survival, under at least two independent renderers.
criteria.test: run the mark build's raster gate under resvg/Chromium and a second engine
criteria.baseline_note: The old kit's marks.py checks only 24px, under one renderer (rsvg-convert, not present on this Mac).

criteria.statement: Every icon artefact ships rounded or circular, per the owner's instruction, except exactly one square unmasked master for Icon Composer -- and that exception is documented, not accidental.
criteria.test: the asset manifest lists every icon artefact's shape; exactly one is 'square-unmasked'
criteria.baseline_note: The old kit ships only a pre-rounded app-icon tile; there is no square unmasked master for Icon Composer at all.

criteria.statement: The kit states, in the owner's own words, that pre-rounding departs from Apple's current guidance, and quotes Apple's stated cost.
criteria.test: the guidebook contains the exact Apple quote about pre-defined masking
criteria.baseline_note: Verified quote to use: "Providing layers with pre-defined masking negatively impacts specular highlight effects and makes edges look jagged."

criteria.statement: visionOS and watchOS icon artefacts are noted as the platforms where the departure costs nothing, because Apple's own system mask there is already circular.
criteria.test: the guidebook states this platform-by-platform, not as a blanket claim
criteria.baseline_note: watchOS canvas is 1088x1088, not 1024 -- confirmed; the old kit's watch asset, if any, must be checked against this, not assumed 1024.

criteria.statement: The Android adaptive icon foreground is NOT pre-rounded; a full-bleed background layer plus an unrounded foreground is supplied so every OEM launcher mask still applies correctly.
criteria.test: the Android asset set has a background layer sized 108x108dp with a foreground logo between 48x48dp and 66x66dp, unrounded
criteria.baseline_note: No adaptive-icon-specific asset exists in the old kit at all -- confirmed dimensions to build to: 108dp canvas, 66dp inner safe zone, 18dp reserved margin per side, logo 48-66dp, monochrome layer for Android 13+ theming.

criteria.statement: Every rasteriser-dependent proof states which renderer(s) produced the figure, so the claim is never presented as renderer-independent fact.
criteria.test: the mark/asset build scripts print their renderer name in the proof output
criteria.baseline_note: marks.py's counter-survival check does not name its renderer in its output.

criteria.statement: No colour role is named after a role Google's current Compose Material3 API marks Deprecated.
criteria.test: cross-reference every --gru-* role name against the ColorScheme API's actual Deprecated annotations, not against a secondhand summary
criteria.baseline_note: CORRECTED FINDING, important: background/onBackground/surfaceVariant are NOT marked Deprecated as properties in the current ColorScheme API -- only two constructor overloads that omit newer parameters are. The old kit's --gru-bg is therefore not importing a formally deprecated name, contrary to what this rebuild's own earlier planning assumed. The naming choice (bg vs surface) is still worth reconsidering for alignment with the newer, larger role vocabulary (10 surface-family roles among 26 total), but it must not be described in the guidebook as 'the deprecated name' -- that claim would itself fail criterion G01.

criteria.statement: Every text pair is proven at 4.5:1 normal / 3:1 large in every theme, with 'large' defined exactly as WCAG defines it (18pt, or 14pt bold) -- not a rounded approximation stated as the standard.
criteria.test: the contrast engine's threshold table cites the exact WCAG definition
criteria.baseline_note: DESIGN-RULES.md §5.1 states "3:1 large (24px, or 19px bold)" -- close but not the standard's own wording (18pt/14pt bold; 19px is this kit's own pixel conversion, not cited as such).

criteria.statement: No AAA claim is made for non-text contrast anywhere, because WCAG defines no AAA level for it.
criteria.test: grep for 'AAA' within 15 words of 'border', 'focus', 'icon', 'non-text', 'target'
criteria.baseline_note: Confirmed: SC 1.4.11 exists only at AA; the Level AAA criteria under Guideline 1.4 (1.4.6, 1.4.7, 1.4.8, 1.4.9) do not cover non-text contrast at all. The old kit makes no AAA-for-non-text claim currently.

criteria.statement: Where the kit states a policy floor above WCAG's normative minimum (e.g. a 7:1 high-contrast-theme floor), it is labelled explicitly as GRU953 policy, not as a conformance claim.
criteria.test: grep for '7:1' and confirm the word 'policy' appears in the same paragraph
criteria.baseline_note: The old kit has no high-contrast theme yet.

criteria.statement: Non-text UI contrast is proven at 3:1 as WCAG's SC 1.4.11 actually states it -- against adjacent colours, not against an arbitrary reference.
criteria.test: the contrast engine's non-text check compares against the actual adjacent colour in context
criteria.baseline_note: Not directly checked against the old engine's implementation in this pass.

criteria.statement: Every tonal surface step has a stated job (background, hover, border, text, etc.), the way Radix Colors' 12-step model and IBM Carbon's Core/Component tokens both do -- not a bare number a reader must look up.
criteria.test: the token doc lists a one-line job for every step
criteria.baseline_note: The old kit's ramps are numbered 50-950 with no stated per-step job.

criteria.statement: Contrast figures are published as the worst legal pairing in the set, not the best one, the way Radix's Lc 60/90 guarantee and USWDS's magic-number floor are both stated as guarantees, not highlights.
criteria.test: CONTRAST.md (or its successor) states a single worst-pair headline figure
criteria.baseline_note: Not directly checked in this pass whether the old CONTRAST.md states a worst-pair headline.

criteria.statement: Every candidate typeface claimed as evaluated appears as a measured row in the type data; the stated count equals the row count.
criteria.test: assert len(candidates measured) == the number claimed in prose
criteria.baseline_note: 05_type/README.md claims 29 candidate families compared; only specimens for 5 (4 rejected + Sora) ship as evidence.

criteria.statement: Bengali shaping is described accurately: Bengali is shaped by its own dedicated OpenType specification (the Indic shaping engine), not blanket-described as shaped 'via the Universal Shaping Engine (USE)'.
criteria.test: grep the kit for 'Universal Shaping Engine' near 'Bengali' and check it is not stated as the shaper actually used
criteria.baseline_note: The old kit does not currently make a claim about which shaping spec governs Bengali; this criterion guards against introducing the imprecise claim during the rebuild.

criteria.statement: Bengali digit usage follows CLDR's own bn-BD convention (native ০-৯ digits, not Western 0-9), and this is stated as sourced from CLDR, not assumed.
criteria.test: grep guidebook for a citation to CLDR bn_BD.xml near any digit-usage rule
criteria.baseline_note: No CLDR citation currently exists for digit choice; confirmed CLDR source: bn (and bn_BD specifically) defaults to native Bengali digits, while bn_IN (India) explicitly overrides to Western digits -- a genuine country-level distinction worth stating precisely.

criteria.statement: The Latin-to-Bangla apparent-size multiplier is a measured figure (from real rendered ink), not an assumed ratio, and is published with the method stated.
criteria.test: the type data file has a measured column, not just an asserted ratio
criteria.baseline_note: No such multiplier is currently measured or published in the old kit.

criteria.statement: Every font's OFL status is checked against the licence's actual current terms (1.1, no 1.2, Reserved Font Name clause worded precisely), not a secondhand paraphrase.
criteria.test: cross-reference each shipped font's licence claim against openfontlicense.org's own text
criteria.baseline_note: The old kit's font licences already correctly cite OFL 1.1 (confirmed: there is no 1.2) and each shipped OFL.txt travels with its font.

criteria.statement: Where a font used for comparison (e.g. Nikosh) has a disputed or unverifiable licence, the kit states the dispute rather than picking one claim to repeat as fact.
criteria.test: grep for 'Nikosh' and confirm the licence is described as disputed/unverified if cited
criteria.baseline_note: The old kit does not currently reference Nikosh; guard for if the typography research phase does.

criteria.statement: Every accessibility floor states the exact WCAG success criterion number it derives from, and platform-specific figures (Apple/Android) are attributed to the platform, not folded into a WCAG citation.
criteria.test: every row in the accessibility table carries an SC id or a named platform, never neither
criteria.baseline_note: DESIGN-RULES.md §5.1's target-size row ("24x24px minimum, 44x44px preferred") cites neither SC 2.5.8 nor a platform by name. Confirmed correct figures to cite: WCAG SC 2.5.8 = 24x24 CSS px; Apple HIG = 44x44pt default / 28x28pt minimum (iOS); Android = 48dp minimum -- three different numbers from three different authorities, never to be conflated.

criteria.statement: Apple-platform components meet Apple's own stated default and minimum control sizes, cited from the current HIG, not a remembered figure.
criteria.test: the component spec states 44x44pt default / 28x28pt minimum, matching the current Buttons and Accessibility HIG pages
criteria.baseline_note: Not directly checked against the old kit's component specs in this pass.

criteria.statement: Where the kit claims Apple 'defers to WCAG' for contrast, this is stated precisely: Apple's Accessibility Inspector tool uses WCAG AA figures (4.5:1 up to 17pt, 3:1 at 18pt+ or any bold) -- it is not stated as a blanket 'Apple publishes no contrast standard at all'.
criteria.test: grep the guidebook for any claim that Apple publishes no contrast figures anywhere, and correct it if so
criteria.baseline_note: Refines the earlier verified-design-standards memory's claim that Apple 'publishes no contrast ratio for text' -- true of the Materials page specifically, false of the Accessibility page, which does cite WCAG AA via Accessibility Inspector. The precise claim is: no PROPRIETARY Apple ratio and none for materials/Liquid Glass specifically, but WCAG AA is cited generally.

criteria.statement: Reduced motion is honoured, and where a duration or curve is stated as a GRU953 choice, it is not attributed to Apple or Google, since neither publishes a duration or named curve.
criteria.test: grep for a millisecond figure or curve name within 15 words of 'Apple' or 'HIG'
criteria.baseline_note: DESIGN-RULES.md §4 states its durations as GRU953's own choice, correctly, and does not attribute them to Apple. Confirmed: Apple's Motion HIG page contains no ms duration and no named easing curve at all -- the only numeric values on the page are a 30-60fps game frame-rate note and a 0.2Hz vestibular-safety caution, neither an animation timing spec.

criteria.statement: Where GRU953 cites Material's motion springs as a model (damping/overshoot behaviour), the actual published parameter values are cited, not an approximate description.
criteria.test: grep for 'spring' near 'Material' and check numeric parameters are cited from source
criteria.baseline_note: The old kit makes no such claim; guard for the rebuild. Confirmed values if cited: expressive spatial springs 0.6-0.8 damping (underdamped/bouncy), expressive effects springs 1.0 damping (critically damped) at every speed.

criteria.statement: lang is declared on every Bangla passage inside an English page, and this is stated as the single highest-value accessibility line for a bilingual brand -- and it is actually true in the shipped markup, not just claimed.
criteria.test: grep every HTML output for Bangla codepoints outside a lang="bn" scope
criteria.baseline_note: DESIGN-RULES.md §5.3 claims this; not directly re-verified against the shipped guidebook markup in this pass.

criteria.group: F - Voice, language and bilingual parity
criteria.statement: Every worked example in the voice guide uses real GRU953 artefacts (real error messages, real byte counts, real history) rather than an invented product and invented figures.
criteria.test: grep 02_strategy/VERBAL-IDENTITY*.md for the word 'Ledger' or other invented-example markers
criteria.baseline_note: VERBAL-IDENTITY.md sections 1, 2, 3 and 6 are built on an imaginary app 'Ledger' with invented figures, self-flagged in the document's own preamble but not marked inline at each occurrence.

criteria.group: F - Voice, language and bilingual parity
criteria.statement: No example changelog or version history reads as real (no real-looking dated headings), matching the kit's own stated position that it has no changelog.
criteria.test: grep for version-number-shaped headings with dates
criteria.baseline_note: VERBAL-IDENTITY.md contains example headings '## 2.4.1 -- 8 August 2026' and '## 2.5.0 -- 3 September 2026' (the second in the future relative to the kit's own build date) that read as real history despite BRAND-SPEC.md stating the kit has none.

criteria.group: F - Voice, language and bilingual parity
criteria.statement: Every sentence containing a number resolves to a computed source (tokens, measurements, findings) or is explicitly marked unverified -- no invented number anywhere.
criteria.test: every numeric sentence in hand-written prose is cross-referenced against a data file
criteria.baseline_note: The 22.46% squircle claim is the flagship instance; VERBAL-IDENTITY.md's invented figures are a second, broader instance of the same failure mode.

criteria.group: F - Voice, language and bilingual parity
criteria.statement: Concrete, testable content rules exist underneath the voice principles (banned words, sentence patterns, numeric caps), the way Atlassian's and GOV.UK's do -- not principles alone.
criteria.test: count concrete Do/Don't rules with a specific trigger (a word, a number, a construction) in the voice guide
criteria.baseline_note: VERBAL-IDENTITY.md has some concrete rules (word lists) but fewer structural ones (sentence-length caps, list-length caps) than Atlassian's page has. Note: the widely-quoted GOV.UK 'reading age 9' figure could NOT be confirmed on GOV.UK's own current primary guidance -- do not cite it as a GOV.UK standard if referencing this model.

criteria.group: F - Voice, language and bilingual parity
criteria.statement: Bangla is written natively for every string that ships, verified against the actual Bangla Academy standard edition that can be dated and sourced (the 2012 revised edition, reprinted January 2015, is the most recent confirmed edition) -- not against an undated web summary.
criteria.test: every cited spelling rule names the edition and, where possible, a page
criteria.baseline_note: No edition citation currently exists in the old kit's Bangla content.

criteria.group: F - Voice, language and bilingual parity
criteria.statement: Every Bangla string's approval is dated after that string's last edit -- editing a string silently invalidates its prior approval.
criteria.test: the Bangla review data has an approval timestamp newer than the string's edit timestamp for every entry
criteria.baseline_note: No Bangla review mechanism exists yet in the old kit.

criteria.statement: Every numeric claim attributed to an external party carries a verbatim quoted line from a primary source read on a stated date.
criteria.test: cross-reference every external numeric claim in the guidebook against findings.json
criteria.baseline_note: This is the rule the 22.46% squircle claim violated -- no such cross-reference exists in the old kit at all.

criteria.statement: Every external URL cited in the kit returns 200 on the day of the build.
criteria.test: a link-liveness check over every .md/.html/.py/.json file
criteria.baseline_note: 01_research/RESEARCH.md's own PolyForm URL is correct (no trailing slash); the trailing-slash 404 form survives only in the _to_delete archive, now moved to the attic, not the shipping kit -- corrected finding from an earlier over-broad claim of mine.

criteria.statement: A claim of 'inferred' confidence (a structural observation with no formal spec, e.g. Meta's brand architecture) is labelled as such in the same sentence as the claim, never presented with the same certainty as a quoted standard.
criteria.test: grep for Meta-attributed claims and confirm each carries an inferred/observed qualifier
criteria.baseline_note: Guard for the Meta section of the new benchmark prose, once written.

criteria.statement: Where a widely-repeated secondary claim could not be confirmed on a primary source (e.g. GOV.UK's 'reading age of 9'), the kit says so explicitly rather than repeating the popular figure as fact.
criteria.test: grep for 'reading age' near 'GOV.UK' and confirm it is marked unconfirmed if present
criteria.baseline_note: Guard for if the plain-language chapter cites this figure.

criteria.statement: A claim about Meta's design-system practice acknowledges Astryx (Meta's own newly public design system, beta since 18 June 2026) rather than asserting Meta publishes nothing comparable to Apple's or Google's design system.
criteria.test: grep for any absolute claim that Meta publishes no design system
criteria.baseline_note: IMPORTANT CORRECTION to this rebuild's own planning assumption: Meta DOES now publish a real, public, open-source design system (Astryx, 150-170+ components, in Beta since 18 June 2026). It is explicitly brand-neutral/white-label, not an expression of Facebook/Instagram/WhatsApp's own visible identity the way HIG/Material are -- so the comparison to Apple/Google must be nuanced (Meta has a design system now, but not one that codifies its own product brand identity), not simply asserted absent.

criteria.statement: Every mechanical gate runs to completion on the owner's own machine from a clean checkout.
criteria.test: sh 00_sandbox/setup.sh && sh scripts/verify-all.sh exits 0
criteria.baseline_note: As of this rebuild's Phase 1 (20 Aug 2026): sh 00_sandbox/setup.sh builds cleanly, smoke.py passes all 8 tools with a real job each, and scripts/no-system-path.sh proves no hidden dependency. Verified on this Mac and on GitHub's Ubuntu CI runner.

criteria.statement: design-system/check.mjs -- the only check that renders and measures the actual cards -- runs in CI on every push, not just locally by chance.
criteria.test: CI job list includes a step calling design-system/check.mjs
criteria.baseline_note: Fixed in this rebuild's Phase 1: wired into .github/workflows/brand.yml job 5. First-ever run: 27 cards, 4 widths x 2 schemes, 216 renders, no findings.

criteria.statement: No generated file contains an absolute path, a timestamp, or a random value.
criteria.test: scan every generated file for date-shaped strings and absolute filesystem paths
criteria.baseline_note: 03_logo/marks.py and lockups.py hardcoded /home/claude/GRU953_Branding/00_sandbox; 04_colour/engine.py hardcoded a GRU953_Build/ path. Fixed in this rebuild's Phase 0 (fork resolution) for the repo copy; root copy retired to the attic.

criteria.statement: Any figure produced by a single rasteriser is confirmed by a second, independent rasteriser before being published as fact.
criteria.test: the mark/asset build runs under two renderers and diffs the result
criteria.baseline_note: The old kit's counter-survival check runs under one renderer only.

criteria.statement: The build works with the system PATH stripped to the minimum needed, and with no fonts installed anywhere on the host, proving no hidden dependency on what merely happens to be on this machine.
criteria.test: sh scripts/no-system-path.sh exits 0
criteria.baseline_note: Built and verified in this rebuild's Phase 1, on both this Mac and GitHub's Ubuntu CI runner -- the hermetic gate caught a real CI configuration bug on its first run anywhere, which was then fixed.

criteria.statement: The kit states plainly that it has had no user research, in contrast to Material 3 Expressive's stated 46 studies / 18,000+ participants, and that this is Google's own unaudited figure with no published methodology.
criteria.test: the guidebook's limits chapter states both figures side by side
criteria.baseline_note: No such comparison exists in the old kit yet.

criteria.statement: The kit never uses an unmeasurable superlative ("gold standard", "world-class", "industry-leading") about itself.
criteria.test: grep the whole tree for these phrases applied to GRU953
criteria.baseline_note: No such phrase currently appears in the old kit's own self-description.
